title: pcell-yeff-cap: cells from noise whose particle-borne link efficiency is selected by intrinsic deaths of cells born low, against an identical-event marker (S,I,D,H)
summary: Revision of the H evidence in 20261025T0820-c06-pcell-multilevel-claim after the reviews of c01, c03 and c09 showed that its death bias was mostly built within each cell's life. Here link yield is a pure efficiency (yeff=1: every catalyst particle draws the same substrate, so yield has no cost inside a cell and helps only the cell), mutation 0.002 per duplication with step 0.1, capped at 1.2, and an inert marker z inherited and mutated the same way. On 4/4 seeds (100000 t from noise) mean yield rises to 1.16-1.18 while the marker ends at 0.85-1.06 (cap_summary.png). Mature-cell deaths (25-41 per run, intrinsic: starvation beside larger neighbours) sit at the 2nd-9th yield percentile of the living cells against 40-63 for the marker. Dying cells born after t=1000 were already below the median at birth (mean birth rank 0.25, 0.28, 0.38, 0.40; marker 0.42, 0.63, 0.43, 0.50). Their own yield falls only 0.03-0.08 during life, against 0.2-0.3 with a replication cost (20261025T0923-c06-pcell-somatic-decline). On the two seeds with most deaths, low-born cells die more often than high-born ones (0.69 vs 0.33 and 0.64 vs 0.36), not on the other two (0.35 vs 0.40, 0.52 vs 0.64). Splits are not selected (mean percentile 0.38-0.58). The population settles at 11-15 cells after t~60000.

claims.statement: In pcell-yeff-cap from an unstructured particle soup, walled cells form and divide (labkit: 9 and 6 persistent splits, generation 2, merge/split 0.06 and 0.25; genealogy 11-16 persistent splits per run, generation 2-3, 0 merges). A heritable link efficiency that arises by mutation rises in the population against an identical-event inert marker on 4/4 seeds (1.16-1.18 vs 0.85-1.06), because the cells that die are the low-yield ones (death percentile 0.02-0.09; marker 0.40-0.63), and they were already low at birth (birth rank 0.25-0.40; marker 0.42-0.63).
claims.track: seed 0, labkit track 53 (pack_seed0/tracks.png, lineage.png): generation 2 (27 -> 50 -> 53), born at t=39500 by a split of track 50, alive to t=100000 while low-yield neighbours die

controls_run.H: data/summary.txt and cap_summary.png: the identical-event inert marker z in the same four runs (same particles, same mutation process, no effect); uncapped and costed arms in parents 20261025T1037-c06-pcell-yeff-response and 20261025T0923-c06-pcell-somatic-decline

claims.limits: Kinds are yield ranks of a continuous trait, not discrete types. The death difference between low- and high-born cells holds on 2 of 4 seeds only; the stronger signal is the death percentile and the mean response against the marker. Dying cells still lose 0.03-0.08 of yield during life (mutation bias at the cap and drift). Higher yield makes bigger cells: the population falls from ~25 to 11-15 cells, and seed 0 carries a giant body (about a quarter of the domain) from t~56000 to ~82000 that breaks up later (pack_seed0/sheet.png); labkit's max/min area ratio of persistent tracks is 12-14. Selection runs only through deaths (splits unselected). Divisions are few (labkit generation 2). The cap ymax=1.2 is imposed; the uncapped arm runs away into giant cells (parent). No dt or resolution test; the L ring is not claimed (B).
